plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the AlexNet convolutional neural network architecture using a 3D volume diagram viewed in perspective. A left-to-right flow begins with a sheared input photograph representing the 224×224×3 input image, followed by a sequence of three-dimensional feature map volumes rendered as parallelogram-faced blocks in light teal (#d3edeb) for the main face and darker teal (#a0d9d3) for the depth layers, while orange (#d18362) and dark orange (#773c23) parallelogram blocks represent convolutional filter kernels applied at each stage. The feature map volumes progressively shrink in spatial resolution while increasing in depth, with labeled dimensions 55×55×96, 27×27×256, and 13×13×384 corresponding to the first three convolutional stages of AlexNet. Ellipsis (…) markers appear within the teal volume stacks to indicate that only a representative subset of the channels is depicted. A “Conv 5×5” annotation above one inter-stage region identifies the kernel size of one convolution, and black arrows with arrowheads indicate the forward data flow between stages. This figure introduces the AlexNet architecture, showing how successive convolution and pooling operations reduce spatial resolution while extracting increasingly abstract feature representations.

elements: Sheared input image slab (photograph of candles) standing at far left, front face spanned by vertical + receding-diagonal axes, tiny thickness for 3 channels
Dimension label '224×224×3' at top with thin leader arrow pointing down-left to the top edge of the input image
Conv1 feature-map block (55×55×96): tall narrow orange parallelepiped
Leader arrow + rotated label '55×55×96' pointing down-right to the Conv1 block
Conv2 feature-map block (27×27×256): near-cubic orange parallelepiped
Leader arrow + rotated label '27×27×256' pointing to the Conv2 block
Conv3 feature-map block (13×13×384): short wide orange parallelepiped
Conv4 feature-map block (13×13×384): identical short wide orange parallelepiped
Conv5 feature-map block (13×13×256): slightly thinner short wide orange parallelepiped
Leader arrow + rotated label '13×13×384' above the Conv3/Conv4 pair
Leader arrow + rotated label '13×13×256' pointing to the Conv5 block
Four light-teal tall thin fully-connected bars: 4096, 4096, 1000, 1000, bottoms aligned on the baseline
Vertical ellipsis dots and zigzag break marks inside each teal FC bar
Labels '4096', '4096', '1000', '1000' above each teal bar
Black forward-flow arrows along the bottom baseline between consecutive stages, angled up-right
Rotated operation labels under the arrows: 'Conv 11×11 / Stride 4', 'MaxPool / Conv 5×5', 'MaxPool', 'Conv 3×3', 'MaxPool + FC', 'FC', 'FC', 'Softmax'
Rectangular bracket connector drawn above the Conv3→Conv4 gap (Conv 3×3 skip-style routing line)
Long rectangular bracket connector running below Conv3–Conv5 for the 'MaxPool + FC' label
Baseline ground line implied by the row of arrows

interactions.label: Animate data flow through the network
interactions.teaches: Activation travels left to right: each conv/pool step visibly shrinks the spatial face (224→55→27→13) while the horizontal channel thickness grows (3→96→256→384), so information is traded from resolution into feature depth.

interactions.label: Convolutional stage
interactions.teaches: Selecting a stage highlights its tensor block and pops an overlay giving that stage's kernel (11×11 stride 4, 5×5, 3×3) and the exact input→output feature-map dimensions, tying each operation to the size change it causes.

interactions.label: Receptive-field overlay
interactions.teaches: One activation cell in the selected block traces back to a patch in the previous block and a much larger patch on the 224×224 input — the receptive field grows in input pixels exactly as the feature-map resolution falls.

demo_steps.title: Input image
demo_steps.narration: The network starts with a 224×224 RGB image, drawn as a thin sheared slab only 3 channels deep.

demo_steps.title: Conv 11×11, stride 4 → 55×55×96
demo_steps.narration: A big 11×11 kernel striding by 4 collapses the spatial face to 55×55 while stacking 96 channels, giving the first tall orange block.

demo_steps.title: MaxPool + Conv 5×5 → 27×27×256
demo_steps.narration: Pooling halves the resolution and a 5×5 convolution widens the volume to 256 channels; the block becomes nearly cubic.

demo_steps.title: MaxPool + Conv 3×3 → 13×13×384
demo_steps.narration: Another pool and 3×3 convolutions leave a short, wide 13×13×384 block: almost no spatial extent, very deep.

demo_steps.title: Receptive field grows
demo_steps.narration: Turn on the overlay: one cell of the 13×13 block already sees most of the original image, even though it is only one of 169 spatial positions.

demo_steps.title: Fully connected head
demo_steps.narration: The final volume is flattened into 4096-, 4096-, 1000-unit vectors (teal bars, ellipses standing for omitted units) ending in a 1000-way softmax.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Axes: +X screen-right (flow direction, carries CHANNEL count), +Y screen-up (carries spatial height), +Z receding diagonal up-right at ~30° screen (carries spatial width). Every volume is an oblique box X(channels) × Y(spatial) × Z(spatial). Sizes are stylised, not linear in the numbers — use exactly: input image 0.08 × 3.40 × 3.40 at x=-7.0, bottom y=0.6 (it floats well above the baseline); Conv1 55×55×96 = 0.50 × 1.15 × 1.15 at x=-4.6, bottom y=0.05; Conv2 27×27×256 = 0.62 × 0.80 × 0.80 at x=-3.0, bottom y=0.05; Conv3 13×13×384 = 0.75 × 0.45 × 0.45 at x=-1.4; Conv4 13×13×384 = 0.75 × 0.45 × 0.45 at x=-0.15 (identical to Conv3 — equal values, equal size); Conv5 13×13×256 = 0.55 × 0.45 × 0.45 at x=1.1; all conv blocks rest with bottom face on y≈0.05. FC bars: thin teal boxes 0.14 × H × 0.14, bottoms aligned at y=0.05, at x = 2.5 (H=3.40, '4096'), x = 3.15 (H=3.40, '4096'), x = 3.85 (H=1.60, '1000'), x = 4.50 (H=1.60, '1000'). Each teal bar carries two horizontal zigzag break marks with three vertical dots between them at mid-height. Colours: conv blocks front/top face #d18362 with darker receding faces and outlines #773c23; FC bars #d3edeb with side faces #a0d9d3, black outlines; input slab is a dark photograph texture (near-black surround, warm orange candle flames) with black border; all text and arrows pure black on white background. Dimension labels sit above-left of their block, rotated ~30° to match the receding diagonal, joined by a thin straight leader arrow to the block's top edge: '224×224×3' top-centre-left, '55×55×96', '27×27×256', '13×13×384' (over the Conv3/Conv4 pair), '13×13×256'. Operation labels are rotated ~35° counter-clockwise and sit below the baseline arrows, in order left to right: 'Conv 11×11 / Stride 4', 'MaxPool / Conv 5×5', 'MaxPool', 'Conv 3×3', 'MaxPool + FC', 'FC', 'FC', 'Softmax'. A thin rectangular bracket connector runs above the Conv3→Conv4 gap and a longer one below Conv3–Conv5. Receptive-field maths: Conv1 11×11 s4 → RF 11px; after pool3 s2 and Conv2 5×5 → RF 51px; after pool and Conv3 3×3 → RF 99px on the 224×224 input.
interactionPlan.notes: Render with an OrthographicCamera plus a cavalier/oblique shear matrix (depth axis projected at 30° screen, depth scale ~0.55) so front faces stay true rectangles; no perspective convergence. Build each volume as a BoxGeometry with flat MeshBasicMaterial faces (slightly darker on +Z/top) plus THREE.LineSegments(EdgesGeometry) in the dark outline colour for the crisp ink look. Input photo as a PlaneGeometry with a CanvasTexture (dark scene with warm candle blobs). Labels and rotated operation text as CSS2DObject/HTML overlays so they stay legible and can be rotated in screen space. Flow animation: an emissive/opacity pulse that walks the block sequence with a moving arrow glow on the baseline, ~0.8 s per stage. Stage slider drives an outline colour swap (highlight #ffd24d) plus an HTML overlay card near the selected block. Receptive-field toggle draws a small filled quad on the selected block's front face and translucent back-projected quads on the previous block and on the input plane, connected by thin dashed lines. Keep depth sorting correct by rendering blocks back-to-front along X.

attempts.html:
AlexNet architecture
Guided tour
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The first conv block (55×55×96) renders yellow/gold by default because stage 1 is pre-selected, whereas in the source all five conv volumes share the same salmon-orange face/terracotta edge scheme — the default view therefore reads as a different colour set.

The floating 'Conv 11×11, stride 4 (+ MaxPool 3×3 s2)' stage card sits on top of the figure and occludes most of the '55×55×96' leader label (only '×96' is readable), clutter that does not exist in the source.

The input photograph is a crude synthetic gradient (a single blurred glow) rather than the recognisable five-candle photo; the slab also lacks the visible sheared side face/thickness that reads as '×3 channels' in the source.
The 'MaxPool + FC', 'FC', 'FC' labels bunch together near x≈2–3 so they read as 'MaxPool + FC FC', less cleanly separated than in the source where each arrow has its own well-spaced caption.

Block proportions drift slightly: in the source conv1 is a markedly tall, thick slab and conv2 a near-cube clearly larger than conv3–5; in the render the size falloff from conv1→conv5 is flatter and conv1 is comparatively small relative to the input plane.
evaluation.notes: A faithful oblique reconstruction of the AlexNet pipeline with correct volumes, arrows, brackets and dimension labels, backed by genuinely useful interactions (stage slider, receptive-field overlay with correct RF arithmetic, data-flow animation, guided tour); main weaknesses are the default yellow highlight on conv1, a floating info card that covers the 55×55×96 annotation, and a cartoonish input image.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; the remaining issues are implementation details — default highlight color, an info card occluding the 55×55×96 label, label spacing/overlap, block proportions, and the crude input image.

interactions.label: Animate data flow through the network
interactions.teaches: Activation travels left to right: each conv/pool step visibly shrinks the spatial face (224→55→27→13) while the horizontal channel thickness grows (3→96→256→384), so information is traded from resolution into feature depth.

interactions.label: Convolutional stage
interactions.teaches: Selecting a stage highlights its tensor block and pops an overlay giving that stage's kernel (11×11 stride 4, 5×5, 3×3) and the exact input→output feature-map dimensions, tying each operation to the size change it causes.

interactions.label: Receptive-field overlay
interactions.teaches: One activation cell in the selected block traces back to a patch in the previous block and a much larger patch on the 224×224 input — the receptive field grows in input pixels exactly as the feature-map resolution falls.

demo_steps.title: Input image
demo_steps.narration: The network starts with a 224×224 RGB image, drawn as a thin sheared slab only 3 channels deep.

demo_steps.title: Conv 11×11, stride 4 → 55×55×96
demo_steps.narration: A big 11×11 kernel striding by 4 collapses the spatial face to 55×55 while stacking 96 channels, giving the first tall orange block.

demo_steps.title: MaxPool + Conv 5×5 → 27×27×256
demo_steps.narration: Pooling halves the resolution and a 5×5 convolution widens the volume to 256 channels; the block becomes nearly cubic.

demo_steps.title: MaxPool + Conv 3×3 → 13×13×384
demo_steps.narration: Another pool and 3×3 convolutions leave a short, wide 13×13×384 block: almost no spatial extent, very deep.

demo_steps.title: Receptive field grows
demo_steps.narration: Turn on the overlay: one cell of the 13×13 block already sees most of the original image, even though it is only one of 169 spatial positions.

demo_steps.title: Fully connected head
demo_steps.narration: The final volume is flattened into 4096-, 4096-, 1000-unit vectors (teal bars, ellipses standing for omitted units) ending in a 1000-way softmax.
